utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-97-24-A, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Appearances of the parties. Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRACOL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President. Xavier Tracol for the Prosecutor with Helen Brady and Susan Grogan, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Branko Lukic for Dr. Stakic this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stakic, I just wanted to make sure that you can hear me and in a language that you understand. Did you understand what I said? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. I can follow in a language that I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. This is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires that a Status Conference be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. Our last Status Conference in this case was on February 23, 2005. Mr. Stakic, I would like to know whether you have any issues that you would like to raise now in relation to your detention, please. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] All I can say is that I continue to receive medical treatment. This has been the case for six months and I'm provided with medicine three times a day. I am managing to keep my blood pressure under control. Occasionally it is 150/90, but on the whole, it is not that high. And I do not have any other problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stakic. You may be seated. At the moment, the parties' submissions on their respective appeals from the trial judgement are complete. While at the last Status Conference I told you that the appeal hearing would likely be scheduled sometime in June, it has for various reasons been necessary to delay. The hearing is now scheduled for the 4th and the 5th of October, 2005. An order to this effect will be issued soon. Although there are two days that we have scheduled for the hearing, I would like to stress that the Appeals Chamber in no way requires that you use all of this time, and indeed we would be grateful if submissions could be made as concisely as possible. I understand that two briefs have been filed confidentially. These are Milomir Stakic re-filed Appellant's brief in support of his notice of appeal filed on the 9th of March 2004 and the Prosecution's response brief filed on 8 April 2004. Pursuant to Rule 78 and 107, the Appeals Chamber requires in addition to any confidential brief that public briefs be filed so as to be able, inter alia, to conduct a public appeal hearing and render a public judgement. In reviewing the briefs filed in this case, the reason for their confidentiality was not immediately apparent to me. Therefore, I would like confirmation and an explanation from the Prosecution and the Defence of the confidential nature of these filings. I turn to the Defence. Mr. Ostojic, could you kindly explain your position on the confidentiality of the briefs?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is Mr. Lukic. I know that it's much easier to remember the big guy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Our confidentiality is actually based basically on use of some closed sessions, transcripts from closed sessions, and we are ready to make public version but probably we'll need up to three weeks to revise this confidential brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: In other words, you could not just make it public, you would have to have a redacted version; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Your Honour, that that's the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Do you need three weeks or do you think I could persuade you to do it in two?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need three weeks, but you can persuade to us do it in two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So I do appreciate your cooperation on that, and I take it that the Defence has agreed to two weeks. And now I turn to the Prosecution. Now, I presume that you -- did you make your brief confidential simply because this was in response to the confidential brief or you had reasons of your own?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRACOL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That's exactly the reason. We responded to the brief of the Defence, and since the brief filed by the Defence was done so confidentially, we filed our brief in response confidentially because the brief refers several times to transcripts that took place in closed session, of hearings that took place in closed session. The Prosecution would be ready to file a redacted version of its brief in response. What we suggest, Your Honour, is to -- for you to grant us the same time that was granted to the Defence in order to file this redacted version of the brief in response, but it might be appropriate for the Prosecution to file this redacted version only after the Defence has filed its own brief in a redacted version, because the brief of the Prosecution depends on the brief filed by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: This problem makes sense to have a sequential, not a concurrent, redaction of your brief, but then I really don't think that if you simply sort of would follow the model of the Defence, that you need two weeks for that, so I suggest that you will make do with one week. Two weeks for the Defence and one week for you to adjust. It should not be too complicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRACOL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We would be in a position to file the redacted version of our brief in response two weeks after the filing by the Defence of its redacted -- of the redacted version of its own brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I'm not sure you understood me. I meant one week after the filing by the Defence. Defence agreed to two weeks. I don't think you need two weeks to --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRACOL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: -- your brief in response, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRACOL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, one week could be appropriate, although two weeks would probably be better but one week would be all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I very much appreciate the cooperation of Mr. Lukic and of Mr. Tracol in adjusting these briefing periods. And is there another question that the Defence or the -- you may be seated, Mr. Tracol. Unless you want to make an argument of anything. Is there anything on which you would, like either the Defence or the Prosecution, any issue which you would like to raise? You would like to, Mr. Tracol, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRACOL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is another issue I'd like to raise today, Your Honour. And that is related to the decision rendered by the Appeals Chamber on the admission of additional evidence on appeal. It's your decision of 25 of January 2005. I note that it is a confidential decision. Therefore, it might be adequate for us to move into closed session in order to discuss the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: That might be prudent to do. We will now go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can see that we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Wait a second. Mr. Registrar, are we in open session now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is nothing on the Defence side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Tracol.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRACOL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No other matters to be raised by the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I thank the parties for their attendance and call the proceedings to a close.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
